subject: Transportation Systems
title: Gap Bridges: Crossing the Impossible
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Gap Bridges: Crossing the Impossible.

hook.text: Engineers dream of bridging the Strait of Messina, the Strait of Gibraltar, and even the Bering Strait.

buildup.text: The Messina crossing would connect Sicily to mainland Italy with a single 2-mile suspension span.

discovery.text: A Gibraltar bridge or tunnel could link Europe to Africa. The strait is 9 miles wide and 2,800 feet deep.

twist.text: Extreme depth, earthquakes, and political complexity have kept every megaproject at the proposal stage.

climax.text: Technology could build them. Politics, money, and maintenance challenges keep these crossings as dreams.

punchline.text: The biggest bridges exist only on blueprints—for now.

quiz.question: Why haven't crossings like the Strait of Gibraltar bridge been built?
options: Extreme depth, earthquakes, cost, and political complexity
